intuition.title: Precursor release and thermodynamic selection
intuition.text: The authors propose that a poorly soluble mixed acetate/oleate cadmium precursor releases reactive cadmium slowly in ODE, making release rate-limiting. The displayed Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ symbols simplify associated reactant species; the paper does not measure free-ion speciation or an exact precursor molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Precursor preparation and proposed mechanism

intuition.title: Feed ratio and family persistence
intuition.text: Low acid/Cd feed favors the proposed mixed cadmium precursor, while high Cd/S is proposed to shift formation toward stable magic-sized products. The authors interpret persistent absorption wavelengths with changing intensities as changes in population, rather than continuous growth of one family into another. These are source interpretations supported by the displayed time courses, not a universally validated kinetic model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 2–3 and mechanistic discussion

intuition.title: Ligand-chain comparison
intuition.text: Replacing oleic acid by octanoic acid yields Family 324 in the displayed comparison. The authors connect shorter-chain acids to smaller stable families, with other supporting examples in cited work. The comparison is not a complete independently tested parameter map; the caption abbreviation conflict is retained.

intuition.title: Surface passivation and bright emission
intuition.text: The paper relates narrow bandgap emission and a small nonresonant Stokes shift to well-defined nanocrystals. Solid-state NMR is interpreted as carboxylate attachment to surface cadmium, with distinguishable surface and core environments. The source does not supply ligand coverage or a coordinate-resolved surface structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–4, Optical results and Figures 4–5

intuition.title: Why size depends on the measurement
intuition.text: The authors attribute larger dried TEM/XRD estimates partly to evaporation-induced aggregation or coalescence. DOSY instead measures a diffusion ratio after redispersion in toluene-d8. The sample was air-dried during its preparation, so the contrast concerns the measurement state rather than a never-dried synthesis. The differently based size estimates should not be averaged.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–6, Figure 6 and characterization methods

intuition.title: Four-step proposed reaction scheme
intuition.text: The authors depict (1) Cd(OAc)2·2H2O + OA → Cd(OAc)(OA); (2) Cd(OAc)(OA) → Cd²⁺; (3) (TMS)2S → S²⁻; and (4) Cd²⁺ + S²⁻ ⇌ (CdS)n (MSQD). Cd²⁺ and S²⁻ are simplified reactant symbols with associated counterions omitted. This is an author-proposed mechanism, not measured free-ion speciation or balanced reaction stoichiometry.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.3, unnumbered four-step scheme and surrounding discussion

general_background.title: Heating and precursor conversion
general_background.summary: As a mixture is heated, precursor conversion and particle growth can change at different rates. Different activation barriers can make these rates change differently as temperature rises, allowing nucleation and growth to overlap.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
